behavior_in_task_description.explanation: This is a bug report built around a video, and its stated expectations line up with what the tests check. The released coins should act like a normal coin burst (both tests that check the burst spreads out), come to rest (landed_coins_come_to_rest and coins_settle_on_floor), and be collected by Tux (released_coins_can_be_collected). Once in the water they should drift down slowly (the floats/sinking tests). The recording shows the details the text leaves out. The tests use behavioural thresholds, not interface details the agent would have to guess.

behavior_in_tests.explanation: Every symptom the instruction describes has its own behavioural test run in the real game binary: the burst spreads to both sides and all coins come out, coins slow down and sink slowly in water (including coins that enter fast and coins that start at rest), landed coins stop instead of sliding or hopping, and Tux can pick up the released coins. Two pass-to-pass tests guard the normal fall through the air.

informative_test_structure.explanation: evaluate_heavycoin.py opens with a docstring that lays out the geometry of both test levels and how the zones are defined. Each test is a named entry with a clear assertion and a detailed failure message. The level scripts are short and print parseable sample lines. test.sh separates the task-specific run_tests block from the generic plumbing.

anti_cheating_measures.explanation: The tests and the solution are not in the image. The injected bug patches are applied and deleted in the same RUN step. Upstream git history is replaced with a single base commit, so the fix commit cannot be reached. File timestamps are flattened so the last-modified file does not point at the bug. The agent has no network access. test.sh restores the test paths before applying hidden test levels that check behaviour in the running game, not the source, so string matching cannot pass them.

structured_data_schema.explanation: The task is a source code fix. It produces no structured output.

pinned_dependencies.explanation: SuperTux is checked out at a pinned base commit, and its submodules are pinned to that commit. Only apt packages are installed, and those don't need pins. There are no unpinned pip packages.

typos.explanation: No typos in the paths, filenames, or test IDs that would break anything. The IDs match across config.json, task.toml, and evaluate_heavycoin.py. test.sh has some leftover comments about wx and passes an undefined REPORTS array to verifier.py, but that array expands to nothing and verifier.py reads JUNIT_OUT, so it is harmless.

tests_or_solution_in_image.explanation: The Dockerfile copies only ca-certificates.crt, the bug patches (deleted right after they are applied), and recording.mp4. Neither tests/ nor solution/ is copied in.

test_deps_in_image.explanation: The image installs only build and runtime dependencies for the game, plus ffmpeg so the agent can inspect the video. The tests need just the game binary they rebuild and python3 from the standard library. No test-only frameworks are baked in.

hardcoded_solution.explanation: solve.sh applies fix.patch, a real source diff across coin.cpp and coin_explode.cpp. It fixes the velocity spread, adds water physics, changes the collision group, and fixes the landing logic. It does not print or echo answers.

file_reference_mentioned.explanation: The agent only edits existing source files, and the tests don't check for any output files.
